lead.title: FCC Opens 450 MHz to Drone C2, Clears 24 GHz Band for Counter-Drone Radar
lead.summary: The Federal Communications Commission adopted final rules on November 19 that open the 450 MHz band for drone command-and-control links and clear the 24 GHz band for ground-based radar to detect unauthorized drones. The order also updates power rules in the 800 MHz air-ground band to improve in-flight broadband services.

The company will keep its initial fleet small while it waits for a next-generation platform with less expensive sensors and computing hardware.

The STAMPEDE initiative includes a contractual option to purchase up to 10,000 aircraft, which does not represent a confirmed purchase.

stories.title: Hyundai Motor to Begin Supplying Robotaxis to Waymo Starting in the Fourth Quarter
stories.summary: Hyundai Motor will begin supplying Ioniq 5 vehicles dedicated to autonomous driving to Waymo starting in the fourth quarter of 2026. The vehicles, produced at the Hyundai Motor Group Metaplant America in Georgia, U.S., are intended to support Waymo's international business expansion starting in early 2027.

stories.title: U.S. Aviation Leaders Link Airspace Modernization to Resilience, Safety and New Aircraft at Washington Summit
stories.summary: The second annual American Aviation Leadership Summit convened in Washington, D.C., shortly after a nationwide ground stop disrupted air travel. More than 60 U.S. aviation organizations urged Congress to add at least $30 billion for air traffic control modernization in a Monday letter.

stories.title: Neural Network Surrogate Predicts Autonomous Fleet Availability and Boosts
stories.summary: Researchers published a study in Discover Artificial Intelligence demonstrating that a backpropagation neural network surrogate accurately models autonomous vehicle availability and raises modeled operating profit by 17.0 percent. The framework improved predictive accuracy by 48.5 percent over conventional analytical benchmarks under degradation-dependent cascading failure rates.

stories.title: Samsung, SK Hynix to develop international standards for semiconductor robots, deploy 10,000 by 2030
San Francisco Waymo passenger finds loaded gun in robotaxi
stories.summary: A San Francisco passenger found a loaded Colt .25 handgun in a Waymo robotaxi on Nov. 17. Waymo reviewed trip data to identify the account holder associated with the terms of service violation and took appropriate action.

stories.title: Indrotek, Robotics, UAV and Counter-UAS Solutions, Files for U.S. National Exchange IPO
stories.summary: Indrocorp Technologies Inc., doing business as Indrotek, filed a Form F-1 to register its initial U.S. public offering of common shares. The company has not disclosed the number of shares, price range, or expected offering proceeds in this preliminary filing.

stories.title: FEV hosts Advanced Robotics Conference on robot deployment
stories.summary: FEV will host the Advanced Robotics Conference on 25–26 November at its headquarters in Aachen, Germany, to discuss industrial deployment, safety, and AI learning. The event features live robot demonstrations, a Hugging Face presentation on LeRobot, and a panel with Schaeffler, RoboStrategy, Fraunhofer IPA, and MYBOTSHOP examining Europe's competitive position in humanoid robotics.

stories.title: Press Release: Quigley, Duckworth and Durbin Respond to FRA Chicago Amtrak Facility Grant Rescoping
Drone Threats Prompt RAF To Install Netting At Bases To Protect Aircraft: Reports
stories.summary: The Royal Air Force is installing Kevlar anti-drone nets to protect aircraft that cannot be placed in hangars or hardened shelters, according to reports from The Times and Sky News. The British Defense Ministry stated it is investing an additional £470 million to strengthen security at military sites, including better physical protection and counter-drone capabilities.

stories.title: MBTA Revisits Its Long-Term Vision for Regional Rail
stories.summary: The MBTA is revisiting its $40.7 billion 2019 “rail vision” plans for the commuter rail system to reflect new post-pandemic and economic realities. In a series of public meetings on November 4th and 17th, the T kicked off its new Regional Rail Modernization planning initiative.

stories.title: FAA expects few near-term changes for helicopters sharing low-altitude airspace
stories.summary: The FAA told Vertical Plus that helicopter operators should expect few changes to day-to-day airspace procedures over the next 12 to 24 months as drone operations expand and piloted eVTOL aircraft prepare to enter service. The agency stated that early piloted eVTOL flights will use established helicopter routes and follow existing visual flight rules and air traffic control procedures.

stories.title: Tesla Cybercab Spotted in Anaheim Hills, California
stories.summary: A gold Tesla Cybercab appeared in Anaheim Hills, California, on November 24, days after the company began offering rides in Dallas. Local resident Steven Silwanis shared video of the two-seater, noting it was his first time seeing one outside Texas, though the clip does not confirm autonomous driving.

stories.title: Angelini Technologies acquires stake in Oversonic Robotics to support international expansion
stories.summary: Angelini Technologies acquired a stake in Oversonic Robotics to support the Italian company's industrial growth and international expansion, with a particular focus on the US market. The investment follows the addition of STMicroelectronics, Fondazione Tech e Biomedical, and SpotInvest to Oversonic's shareholder base in June 2026, while financial terms and the size of the stake were not disclosed.

stories.title: US Marines debut 10 Archer attack drones for first time in seven-month rotation
stories.summary: The Marine Rotational Force-Darwin deployed 10 Archer first-person-view strike drones and the Tactical Resupply Unmanned Aircraft System to Australia for the first time during its seven-month rotation. Around 2,000 Marines served on the deployment, which included training in New Caledonia, French Polynesia, the Philippines, and Papua New Guinea.

stories.title: 3D-printed robotic hand cuts complexity without sacrificing dexterity
stories.summary: Associate professor Cong Wang and doctoral student Neel Adwani designed the PHD Hand, a 3D-printed robotic hand that uses off-the-shelf servos and springs to reduce cost and maintenance compared to commercial options. The team released files, videos, and complete instructions on the project website, with future work focused on manipulating real-world objects and integrating tactile sensing.

stories.title: JATEC Project Targets 3D Printing for Drone Repair and Component Supply
stories.summary: The NATO-Ukraine Joint Analysis, Training and Education Centre (JATEC) is running a project to develop additive manufacturing systems for unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) to support rapid repair and component supply. The initiative aims to apply Ukraine’s battlefield experience to defense capabilities developed with NATO partners, including training specialists and building an expert community for practical military solutions.

stories.title: Meta-Learning and Physics Model Accurately Predicts Ducted eVTOL Ground
stories.summary: A research team developed a physics-inspired data-driven model that predicts transient, non-linear in-ground-effect thrust fluctuations in ducted-fan electric vertical take-off and landing aircraft. Experimental evaluations revealed the model achieved mean relative errors of 1.1 percent on training tasks and 0.7 percent on testing tasks.

stories.title: Tesla Expands Robotaxi in Dallas and Cuts Fares
stories.summary: Tesla expanded its Dallas Robotaxi service area north of University Park toward Farmers Branch, Addison, and Richardson on November 25, adding more cars and lowering fares ahead of Thanksgiving. The company did not specify the new flat fare or the duration of the lower pricing.

also.title: Tesla nearly doubles Dallas Robotaxi coverage just one week after Cybercab launch

stories.title: EU proposes adding one of Russia’s smallest drone manufacturers to its 22nd sanctions package
stories.summary: The EU proposed adding Ural-based drone maker Vertikal and its director Janis Steinbergs to the 22nd sanctions package. The draft also includes Rosatom enterprises, International Boxing Association president Umar Kremlev, and First Deputy Prime Minister Denis Manturov.

stories.title: No Starlink, no problem, part deux: Ukrainian student invents autopilot system for UAV that works without GPS, receives "The future of Ukraine" presidential award
stories.summary: Yaroslav Sheiko, an 11th-grade pupil from Poltava, received the presidential distinction known as "The Future of Ukraine" for his engineering achievements. His work includes an artificial intelligence-powered flight control system and optical-electronic stabilization technology designed for unmanned aerial vehicles.

stories.title: Tesla Plans Steering-Wheel-Free Model Y for Larger Robotaxi Groups
stories.summary: Tesla CEO Elon Musk said the company is considering a driverless Model Y without a steering wheel or pedals to transport six or seven people, as the current two-seater Cybercab serves most passenger trips. Musk did not provide a launch date, pricing, or details on how the vehicle would meet requirements for operation without conventional driver controls.

also.title: Tesla to Equip Model Y With Starlink for Robotaxi Service

stories.title: Joby Aviation Jumps 9% as Air Taxi Stocks Defy Tech Selloff; Archer Aviation Rallies 7%, EHang Rises 6%
stories.summary: Joby Aviation stock rose 9% to $3.83 on November 25, outpacing Archer Aviation and EHang as technology shares sold off. The company previously raised its full-year 2026 revenue guidance to $135 million to $140 million and reported a Q3 per-share loss of $0.22, beating expectations.

stories.title: Will Poland buy counter-drone lasers? A deal could be reached within a few months
stories.summary: Polish Defence Minister Kosiniak-Kamysz said an agreement to acquire counter-drone lasers could be signed within the next few months. The Armament Agency plans preliminary market consultations for two directed-energy systems, one engaging targets at least one kilometre away and the other at no less than 3 km.

stories.title: Pentagon Budgets Up to $500 Million for Extended Range Drone Strike Program
stories.summary: The Defense Innovation Unit opened a solicitation for the Extended Range Strike Gauntlet II program, budgeting up to $500 million for prizes and development. The competition is open to domestic and international companies, with demonstrations planned for March 2027 and a third round in August 2027.

stories.title: New UK Defense Trade Group Aims to Accelerate Adoption of Autonomous Systems
stories.summary: Autonomous UK launched on November 25 with 16 founding members to speed the adoption of autonomous systems across the United Kingdom. The organization, which includes Delta Quad and Saronic, outlined five priorities: funding, procurement, testing, certification, and scaling production.

also.title: DeltaQuad Joins Autonomous UK, New Defense Autonomy Trade Body
DeltaQuad joins Autonomous UK as founding member

stories.title: ARX Robotics says GEREON is first ground robot to join British Army targeting network
stories.summary: ARX Robotics said its GEREON became the first ground robot to connect to the British Army’s AI-enabled targeting network during Exercise Haraka Storm in Kenya. The German company said the Army took a tenth as long to detect a target, decide how to respond and act during the trial.

stories.title: FCC Opens 450 MHz to Drone C2, Clears 24 GHz Band for Counter-Drone Radar
stories.summary: The Federal Communications Commission adopted final rules on November 19 that open the 450 MHz band for drone command-and-control links and clear the 24 GHz band for ground-based radar to detect unauthorized drones. The order also updates power rules in the 800 MHz air-ground band to improve in-flight broadband services.

stories.title: Building Together: A New Model for U.S. Defense Drone Manufacturing
stories.summary: XMX Defense announced that seven companies committed to the Texas Unmanned Systems Defense Center of Excellence at Mineral Wells Regional Airport, with four others in discussions. The privately led initiative offers shared testing infrastructure, manufacturing capabilities, and workforce development to accelerate defense technology production.

stories.title: Russian deputy PM says protecting utilities from Ukrainian drones is a top priority this winter
stories.summary: Russian Deputy Prime Minister Marat Khusnullin told lawmakers that protecting utility infrastructure from Ukrainian drone attacks is a top priority this winter, noting that some power and heating plants in and around Moscow are now covered with anti-drone nets.

stories.title: How Vention is cutting factory programming from weeks to minutes
Humble Robotics Raises $51 Million for Cabless Trucks
stories.summary: Humble Robotics raised $51 million, bringing its total funding to $75 million, to develop the Humble Hauler, a cabless Class 8 autonomous truck. The San Francisco startup plans initial customer pilots for 2027 and broader scaling for 2028, targeting short routes between ports, factories, and warehouses.

stories.title: IITs to add 6,000 seats in Robotics, Physical AI and Space Technology over 10 years
stories.summary: The Bhupat and Jyoti Mehta Family Foundation will add 6,000 seats in Robotics, Physical AI, and Space Engineering Technology across multiple IITs over eight to ten years. The initiative includes 5,000 seats for Robotics and Physical AI and 1,000 for Space Engineering, supported by more than 120 dedicated faculty members.

stories.title: Cabinet relaxes drone alert regulations for businesses
stories.summary: The Ukrainian government extended the transition period for businesses to comply with drone threat shelter requirements through June 4, 2027, the Economy Ministry announced on Nov. 25. Businesses that have not yet provided access to shelters may continue operating with employees' consent and while implementing organizational safety measures.

stories.title: Confirmed | This Latin American country is investing $7 billion in its capital's first subway line: It will use Chinese trains, 100% electric and driverless
stories.summary: Colombia is investing nearly $7 billion in Bogota's first subway line, which will use 30 driverless, electric trains made by CRRC. Mayor Carlos Fernando Galan confirmed on Nov. 15, 2026, that the project is 84.68% complete, with commercial service targeted for March 2028.

stories.title: Zelensky reports Ukrainian drone strike on Russian military airfield
stories.summary: Volodymyr Zelensky reported that Ukrainian drones struck a Russian military airfield, with damage still being assessed. He stated that Russian aircraft, military ships, and vessels carrying Russian weapons are legitimate targets for Ukraine.

stories.title: Omni X Emerges From Stealth With AI Built to Protect Cities and Soldiers From Drone Threats
stories.summary: Omni X emerged from stealth on Nov. 25, 2026, announcing its agentic operating system is ready for deployment with defense, government, and public safety clients. The company launched two product lines: IRIS, a counter-drone system for individual soldiers, and a civic platform for cities, airports, seaports, and stadiums.

stories.title: France's Vinci raises stake in Lisea, values high-speed rail operator at â¬2.1 billion
stories.summary: French infrastructure group Vinci raised its stake in Lisea, the operator of the South Europe Atlantic high-speed rail line between Tours and Bordeaux, to 50.04% by buying an additional 8.0% from state-owned Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations. The deal values Lisea's equity at €2.1 billion ($2.30 billion), and Vinci said Lisea would be little affected by any increase in the long-distance infrastructure tax under consideration in France's 2027 finance bill.

stories.title: When One Robot Learns, Can a Thousand Others Follow?
stories.summary: NVIDIA introduced GR00T 2 in November 2026, a model designed to predict future states and control robotic systems using pretraining data that includes more than 400,000 hours of egocentric video. In one experiment, a robot with two five-fingered hands achieved a 65% success rate placing filter paper into a funnel after observing only human demonstrations.

stories.title: Motional prepares for Uber robotaxi launch in Las Vegas
stories.summary: Motional plans to begin offering fully driverless rides through Uber in Las Vegas in early December, after spending two years overhauling its autonomous driving technology. The company will keep its initial fleet small while it waits for a next-generation platform with less expensive sensors and computing hardware.

stories.title: Embention and the Polish Naval Academy (AMW) Sign a Memorandum of Understanding on Unmanned Systems
stories.summary: Embention and the Polish Naval Academy (AMW) signed a Memorandum of Understanding to establish a framework for technical training on Veronte Autopilot, knowledge exchange, and research exploration in unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) and unmanned surface vehicles (USVs). The agreement creates a direct channel between industry and naval education, with specific lines of work to be defined jointly and subject to separate agreements.

stories.title: Robin Radar supports airspace security at Formula 1 Las Vegas Grand Prix in partnership with LVMPD
stories.summary: Robin Radar Systems partnered with the Las Vegas Metropolitan Police Department to support counter-unmanned aircraft system operations during the Formula 1 Las Vegas Grand Prix. The IRIS counter-drone radar integrated into Dedrone’s command-and-control system at the Southern Nevada Counterterrorism Center, providing real-time situational awareness and 360-degree coverage of the race site. The deployment contributed to a successful security operation with no reported drone incursions or hostile aerial activity disrupting the event.

stories.title: FCC should focus on robot security, not country of origin
stories.summary: David Pinn, CEO of Brain Corp, argues the FCC should regulate robot security based on software control rather than country of origin. He states that Brain Corp's technology runs more than 50,000 robots on six continents and has logged more than 25 million hours of autonomous operation.

stories.title: US military drone range could increase as special forces test lithium-sulfur batteries
stories.summary: Li-S Energy shipped 10Ah lithium-sulfur power cells to SOFWERX, a Florida-based non-profit innovation hub working with United States Special Operations Command, to test if the lighter batteries can outperform conventional cells in demanding military environments.

stories.title: RAF plans to build anti-drone nets at UK bases as aircraft 'are moved into hardened hangars overnight to keep them safe'
stories.summary: The Royal Air Force is fortifying its bases with anti-drone nets and hardened hangars as part of a £470 million security overhaul. The Ministry of Defence stated it is investing an additional £470 million to strengthen physical protection, surveillance, and counter-drone capabilities at military sites.

also.title: UK military ‘moving aircraft to hangars in case of drone attacks’
RAF reportedly moving aircraft into hangars amid drone threat concerns

stories.title: BETA Technologies, Surf Air Mobility and Hawaiian Airlines Demonstrate All-Electric ALIA Aircraft at Honolulu Airport
stories.summary: BETA Technologies, Surf Air Mobility and Hawaiian Airlines demonstrated the all-electric ALIA aircraft at Daniel K. Inouye International Airport in Honolulu in June to assess interisland cargo service. The aircraft, built in Vermont, carries up to 200 cubic feet of cargo and uses a mobile Mini Cube charging unit while permanent infrastructure develops.

stories.title: Ukraine Achieves World First by Downing Jet-Powered Drone With Combat Laser
stories.summary: Ukraine shot down a jet-powered 'Geran' drone using the Blysk air defense laser system developed by Carmin Sky. Serhii Beskrestnov, an advisor to President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, announced the intercept on November 25, noting that trials are ongoing to protect critical infrastructure facilities.

Justice Department Clarifies Drone Detection Legal Limits
stories.summary: The Department of Justice issued a legal opinion on November 25, 2026, concluding that law enforcement may deploy acoustic, electro-optical, infrared, radar, and radiofrequency systems to detect unmanned aircraft. The Office of Legal Counsel determined that radiofrequency spectrum monitoring generally does not violate the Wiretap Act, while technologies capturing communication contents remain subject to statutory limits.

also.title: Dept. of Justice issues opinion on drone detection practices

stories.title: Did Russia use Nvidia hardware in drone that killed civilians in Ukraine? What we know
stories.summary: Ukrainian officials reportedly found Nvidia Jetson Orin modules in Russian drones, including one that killed three civilians in Zaporizhzhia on July 6. Snopes left the claim unrated due to a lack of primary evidence from Russia, while Nvidia stated its modules are not available in Russia and are not designed for military purposes.

stories.title: Bedrock Robotics Valued at $4.1 Billion
stories.summary: Bedrock Robotics closed a $600 million Series C round co-led by CapitalG and Emergence Capital, valuing the startup at $4.1 billion. The company sells self-driving kits retrofitted onto excavators and worksite vehicles, with commercial deployments across the United States.

stories.title: State pushing for new regulations to promote drone use
stories.summary: The state government is funding new drone programs for package and medical deliveries. The Department of Transportation partnered with the Michigan Economic Development Corp. and the Department of Labor and Economic Opportunity to create the Advanced Air Mobility Activation Fund in 2025.

stories.title: Tesla Stock Drops More Than 5% As EU Delays Self-Driving Vote And SpaceX Merger Talks Rattle Investors
stories.summary: Tesla shares fell 5.18% Wednesday after the European Union postponed its vote on the company's driver-assistance software to Dec. 15. Investors also reacted to reports of merger talks with SpaceX and a broad sell-off in technology stocks.

also.title: Tesla Slides 6% as EU Delays Vote on Its Self-Driving Software; Rivian and Lucid Drop 4%

EU postpones meeting on Tesla's autonomous driving system

stories.title: NS launches second-hand train sales portal as EU closes competition inquiry
stories.summary: The European Commission closed a preliminary antitrust investigation into Dutch passenger operator NS after the company launched a second-hand rolling stock sales portal.

stories.title: BAE Systems, RENK, and Forterra Develop Autonomous AMPV for the US Army
EU Drone Wall Due in December as Leak Puts Most Defenses Past 2030
stories.summary: The European Drone Defence Initiative is due to reach initial capacity by the end of December, with full operation expected a year later. A leaked European Defence Agency report indicates that only about a third of member states' counter-drone programs are expected to deliver by the end of the decade, despite €18.9 billion in investment between 2024 and 2029.

stories.title: Royal Navy picks HII for mine hunting drone fleet
stories.summary: Defence Equipment and Support published a notice describing the procurement of eight mine hunting mission systems, including unmanned underwater vehicles, valued at £303 million excluding VAT. The award decision was made on 3 November, with a revised estimated contract start date of Wednesday 25th November 2026.

stories.title: Ukrainian Air3F Unveils T-Bone Digital Ground Control Station for FPV Drones
stories.summary: Ukrainian company Air3F presented the T-Bone Digital, a new digital ground control station for unmanned aerial vehicles that supports high-resolution video transmission. The station is built around the Walksnail Ascent digital video transmission system and consists of an operator’s case with a 19-inch monitor and a remote Viper antenna unit.

stories.title: Türkiye’s Aselsan integrates laser-guided Tolun L munition onto Bayraktar Akinci drone in live-fire test
stories.summary: Turkish defense firm Aselsan successfully integrated its 250-pound-class Tolun L laser-guided munition onto a Bayraktar Akinci drone during a live-fire test. The trial marked the first time the Tolun L had been integrated onto a drone platform, according to the manufacturer.

stories.title: Americans Are Taking the Train in Record Numbers. Is US Rail Ready?
stories.summary: Amtrak recorded 37.1 million passenger trips in the 2026 financial year, a 7.4% increase on the previous year, as demand for rail travel in the US continues to grow. The record comes amid a major programme of fleet replacement and infrastructure investment, which hopes to pave the way for accommodating a larger passenger rail market in the US.

also.title: Amtrak Records Highest Ridership in Its History

stories.title: Vietnam sets late 2028 groundbreaking for $67.3 billion North-South bullet rail
Russia Outbuys Ukraine For Chinese Drone Fiber As Prices Jump Sixfold
stories.summary: Russia outbids Ukraine for Chinese optical fiber as prices jump sixfold to nearly $30 per kilometer, according to a Financial Times report. Russian buyers secure the limited supply through centralized, large-volume direct agreements, while Ukraine’s fragmented purchasing across hundreds of companies leaves it at a disadvantage.

stories.title: Kodiak delivers first Western Star trucks for Atlas Energy’s growing autonomous fleet
stories.summary: Kodiak delivered the first Western Star trucks equipped with its seventh-generation hardware to Atlas Energy Solutions, bringing the company's autonomous fleet to 37 trucks operating in the Permian Basin. The new platform offers 50% more computing power, and Atlas ordered 100 trucks in April 2025 after Kodiak reached specific milestones.

also.title: Kodiak Delivers Driverless Western Stars to Atlas

stories.title: Judge Blocks Trump's Arch, Calls Its Drone Defense Claim Not Credible
Einride eyes $250M in ’27 revenues, cash flow milestone the year after
stories.summary: Einride executives forecast the company will finish 2027 with annualized revenues of $250 million, up from roughly $90 million in 2026, and break even on a cash flow basis in 2028. The Stockholm-based firm expects its fleet to reach about 800 trucks by the end of next year, with two-thirds of the projected 2027 revenue covered by longer-term contracts.

stories.title: Army Advances STAMPEDE Drone Manufacturing Initiative
stories.summary: The US Army Contracting Command is coordinating contract awards for the assembly of 400 drone systems and 20 ground control systems to support the Drone Dominance Gauntlet scheduled for March 2027. The STAMPEDE initiative includes a contractual option to purchase up to 10,000 aircraft, which does not represent a confirmed purchase.

stories.title: Pentagon Looks to Auto Industry to Scale US Drone Manufacturing
stories.summary: The Pentagon held preliminary discussions with Ford, General Motors, and Magna to expand US drone production by leveraging automotive supply chains for motors and components. Reuters confirmed Ford discussed military vehicles and satellites with the Pentagon, though no agreements have been announced.

stories.title: Japan’s Black AI Secures Seed Funding to Develop Full-Stack Humanoid Robots
stories.summary: Japanese humanoid robotics startup Black AI secured seed funding from Incubate Fund to develop robots and AI systems for manufacturing environments. The Tokyo-based company will use the investment to speed up humanoid development, expand research into general-purpose robot intelligence, and recruit additional personnel.

stories.title: Ericsson demonstrates tactical 5G connectivity for counter-drone systems during Spanish exercise
stories.summary: Ericsson demonstrated tactical 5G connectivity for counter-drone systems during Spain’s ATLAS 26 exercise from 19 to 23 October at the Médano del Loro training area in Huelva. The deployment used Ericsson’s Ultra Compact Core on frequencies reserved exclusively for military use, enabling wireless data exchange between sensors, radars, command posts and effectors without fixed cabling.

stories.title: U.S. Senate Pushes New Counter-Drone Defenses for Abrams Tanks Amid Evolving Battlefield Threats
Dynamic Aerospace Systems (OTCQB: BRQL) Expands IP with Three Breakthrough Patents for Advanced Autonomous UAV/ Drones
stories.summary: Dynamic Aerospace Systems Corporation formally filed three provisional patent applications covering battery arm designs, parachute recovery systems, and cell compression for autonomous drones. The company stated these innovations address flight endurance, reliability, and safety priorities in the commercial UAV sector.

stories.title: Heavy-Lift Drones Deliver Over 55 Tonnes of Solar Panels to Bentley Motors’ Paint Shop in Believed UK First
stories.summary: AutoSpray Systems used heavy-lift drones to deliver over 55 tonnes of solar panels to Bentley Motors’ Paint Shop in Crewe, a UK first for onshore rooftop construction logistics. The operation moved approximately 10 tonnes daily using the XAG P150 Max under a UK Civil Aviation Authority Operational Authorisation.

stories.title: Putnam Sheriff's Draft Drone Policy Puts ICE Behind a Judge's Warrant
stories.summary: Putnam County Sheriff Brian Hess presented a draft Drone as First Responder policy to the Putnam County Legislature’s Protective Services Committee on November 18 in Carmel, New York. The draft states that Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) needs a judge’s warrant to receive drone video, and Hess wants the drones flying by April 2027 at a cost of $1.3 million over five years.

stories.title: SCARA Robot Market: Why Electronics And Automotive Makers Are Turning To Fast, Compact Automation
stories.summary: The SCARA Robot Market value stood at USD 11.00 billion in 2025 and is anticipated to grow to USD 27.26 billion by 2035, growing at a CAGR of 9.50% in the forecast period of 2026-2035. Four-axis robots held around 64.60% of the market by axis count, while the electronics and semiconductor industry accounted for 40.10% of total demand in 2025.

stories.title: Veronte Autopilot 4x 2.2: 10x Power and Improved Reliability
stories.summary: Embention announced Veronte Autopilot 4x 2.2, a triple-redundant flight control computer for defense drones, civil drones, and eVTOL, available for order now. The unit features ten times the processing power and memory of the 4x 1.8, dissimilar processors, and is designed for DAL A certification.

stories.title: Spotting drones can be harder than downing them, Latvia says
Minister confirms progress on carrier drone wingman trials
stories.summary: Minister for Defence Readiness and Industry Luke Pollard confirmed that Northrop Grumman’s TALON demonstrator will prepare for trials next year in UK waters, including launching from a Queen Elizabeth Class aircraft carrier. The First Sea Lord announced the plan at the International Sea Power Conference on 10 November 2026, stating he would sign a statement of intent with Northrop Grumman aboard HMS Prince of Wales.

stories.title: Council Committee Backs Permanent Police Drone Program After Seven-Week Pilot

stories.summary: Tesla's Texas Robotaxi roster now includes 822 Cybercabs and 734 Model Ys, totaling 1,556 vehicles. Cybercab rides are available in limited parts of Austin and Dallas, with the company announcing the vehicle's arrival in Dallas on November 19.

stories.title: Germany Uses Attack Drones to Strike Russian-Style Tanks in First Live-Fire Exercise
stories.summary: The German armed forces conducted their first live-fire exercise involving attack drones at the Rudninkai military training area in Lithuania, using kamikaze drones from Helsing and Stark to strike Leopard 2 tanks. The Bundeswehr plans to have its own drone regiment fully operational by 2029, with 350 personnel expected by 2027.

stories.title: Türkiye inducts Kizilelma unmanned fighter jet, but how does it compare with its rivals?
stories.summary: Türkiye delivered its first three Kizilelma unmanned combat jets to its armed forces, moving the Baykar-developed program from development into initial military service. stories.title: NATO holds Baltic counter-drone drills with jets from four nations and Lithuania’s NASAMS
stories.summary: NATO’s Allied Air Command led counter-drone drills in the Baltic region from 17 to 19 November, coordinating fighter jets from Belgium, Finland, Italy, and Turkey with Lithuania’s NASAMS ground-based air defence system. The exercise used real drones to help air and ground crews refine shared procedures for responding to threats ranging from one-way attack drones to larger remotely piloted aircraft.

stories.title: EagleNXT books drone orders in seven countries, including in Africa
stories.summary: EagleNXT announced on 12 November 2026 that it sold drones to seven countries across North America, Latin America, Europe, and Africa in a single week. stories.title: Growth of the Autonomous Driving Services Market Driven by Increasing Applications and Rising Demand
stories.summary: The autonomous driving services market is projected to grow from $3.47 billion in 2025 to $13.03 billion by 2030, driven by the commercialization of robotaxi services and autonomous freight transport.

stories.title: Ports of Jersey Leads Work on Island's Counter-Drone Capability After Airport Drone Incidents
stories.summary: Ports of Jersey is leading ongoing work on the island's ability to respond to unauthorised drone activity, Home Affairs Minister Senator Helen Miles said. The update followed incidents at Jersey Airport that led to specialist assistance being sought from UK agencies.

stories.title: Volatus Aerospace signs contract for scheduled drone cargo service in North America
stories.summary: Volatus Aerospace signed a contract announced on 24 November to operate a scheduled drone cargo service for an unnamed North American logistics company. The agreement uses the Canary aircraft, which carries up to 5 kg over 30 km, to make up to six round trips per day between two customer locations.

stories.title: OneSky launches FIMS-connected airspace authorisation services in Australia
stories.summary: OneSky is now providing digital airspace services to eligible commercial drone operators in Australia through its connection to Airservices Australia’s Flight Information Management System (FIMS). The platform provides Automated Airspace Authorisations for eligible operations within three nautical miles of 28 civil controlled aerodromes.

stories.title: Boston Logan Airport Is Testing Self-Driving Wheelchairs and Cleaning Robots Ahead of 2027 Expansion
stories.summary: The Massachusetts Port Authority (Massport) is testing four autonomous cleaning robots from CenoBots in pre-security areas across all terminals at Boston Logan International Airport. Massport CEO Rich Davey stated the agency is seeking information from autonomous wheelchair manufacturers to expand that service next year, noting Logan's narrow corridors prevent the use of golf carts.

stories.title: Senate Panel Seeks Briefing on Autonomous Air Defense
stories.summary: The Senate Armed Services Committee's report accompanying the FY2027 National Defense Authorization Act requests a briefing from the Secretary of the Air Force by March 31, 2027. The briefing will cover autonomous and semi-autonomous air-to-air defense capabilities against drones and cruise missiles.

stories.title: Russia issued flight ban ahead of Romanian F-16 strike on Black Sea drone
stories.summary: Former Romanian Defense Minister Radu Miruță revealed that Romanian Air Force F-16s engaged an explosive-laden maritime drone near the Neptun Deep offshore gas project on August 20, 2026, despite a Russian flight ban announced shortly after the order to engage. Miruță stated the operation pushed legal boundaries outside Romania’s territorial waters and risked a military response from Moscow, which did not occur.

stories.title: Path2 develops online robot cell builder to make automation more accessible
stories.summary: UK robotics software startup Path2 is developing a browser-based robot cell design and programming platform to help smaller manufacturers automate production without substantial systems integration budgets. The platform currently supports 20 Kuka robot models with payload capacities ranging from 20 to 800 kg, with support for ABB, Fanuc, Universal Robots and other major robot manufacturers planned. Path2 plans to charge £495 for an individual robot cell design package, while a subscription costing £99 per month will provide access to unlimited cell design packages.

stories.title: AI Software Aims to Keep Military Drones on Course Through Jamming
stories.summary: SPARC AI launched its Overwatch Positioning Network in August 2026, a software service that helps military drones determine location without GPS by processing existing flight telemetry. stories.title: EU plans rapid response force, counter-drone measures to secure eastern borders

stories.summary: Czech jet engine maker PBS Aerospace aims to double its U.S. production capacity, planning to allocate around $100 million to boost output at its Roswell, Georgia facility. stories.summary: MTR Corporation received three awards at the Hong Kong ICT Awards 2026 for its NEX-T drone tunnel inspection system and Smart Light Rail 2.0 platform. stories.title: Iran Claims Second US MQ-9 Drone Shot Down Near Hormuz
stories.summary: Iran's military claimed it shot down a US MQ-9 drone east of the Strait of Hormuz, stating its air defense systems targeted and destroyed the aircraft. stories.summary: Russian forces launched 112 drones from multiple locations inside Russia and occupied territories, striking 18 sites in Ukraine on Nov. 25. stories.title: Waymo and Tesla Test Robotaxis in Detroit Ahead of Michigan Winter
stories.summary: Waymo plans to open robotaxi rides to the public in Detroit in 2027, the company told Axios Detroit on Thursday, Nov. 19. No launch date has been picked. Testing without human safety drivers began in October. Before that, specialists sat behind the wheel for several months. Now the company is preparing for its first winter in the city with no one driving, WXYZ reported when that phase began. Detroit has become a testing ground for rival robotaxi systems. Michigan's winters could change how fast either one grows. Tesla has joined the local testing. About two dozen gold Cybercabs run out of a Southfield facility, according to the Detroit News. Waymo's cars have no one at the wheel, but the Cybercabs do. Human test drivers steer them with temporary steering wheels. Snow, ice, and freezing temperatures make driving harder for everyone, and robotaxis are no exception. Their sensors can struggle when the weather turns bad. Henry Liu leads the University of Michigan's Mcity autonomous vehicle research center. He told Axios that winter weather is a "manageable challenge" for driverless vehicles, but that it makes running them more complicated. Waymo says its latest technology has heated sensors, micro-wipers, and systems that identify changes in road traction. Safety questions are piling up for the company across the country. California regulators banned its driverless vehicles from freeways after incidents near construction zones and highway patrol vehicles. Waymo then stopped fully driverless freeway trips in all of its markets. Spokesperson Chris Bonelli told Axios the pause won't touch Detroit, since the company hadn't started driverless freeway trips there yet.
